title: The suite keeps only the 25 critical test ids and records every dropped one
goal: every test id outside the keep list of gate keep goes: _tools/test_backlog_portable.py, _tools/test_bench.py, _tools/test_forge.py, _tools/test_land_e2e.py and _tools/test_live_kb.py are deleted, and in _tools/test_check_programs.py, _tools/test_redact.py, _tools/test_prepush_e2e.py and _tools/test_sync_e2e.py each test outside the list goes with the helpers only it used; the suite then collects exactly the 25 kept ids in 9 files and they pass; _tools/test_ids_dropped.txt gets one reason line naming decision D-2tq4fhgs and every dropped id, and _tools/test_ids_baseline.txt holds the 25 kept ids; kb/_self/code.md, kb/_self/tools.md and kb/_self/querylog.md name no deleted test; no test id is added and no tool or kb article changes. Code-lane paths (_tools/): done and the push to main come after its merge request merges (backlog.py land ID --wait-merge 1800).

gates.question: Which test ids stay in the suite under the operator's test policy (D-2tq4fhgs), and which go? Today: 87 ids in 14 files, about 298 s summed and 50 s wall in one profiled run on this loaded host (29 to 31 s wall on the last plain runs).
options: Keep 25 ids in 9 files, drop 62: all of test_authority.py (4: gate classes and operator-only answers), the 2 ids of the file that tests the operator-only suite limits of tests.py, test_kbingest_guards.py (3: untrusted repository), test_leaks.py (3: the leak scan), the 3 ids of the end-to-end file of kbgit's projection command (what leaves for the public home, refused on a leak or a CI verdict that is not ok); in test_check_programs.py the program allowlist and drift's read-only forms (2), in test_redact.py the redactor, distill, the closed ops-row shape and the store check (4), in test_prepush_e2e.py the query-log history refusal and the lane refusal (2), in test_sync_e2e.py the red gate and the code-lane branch (2); test_backlog_portable.py, test_bench.py, test_forge.py, test_land_e2e.py and test_live_kb.py go whole (the lookup eval, check.py and build_index stay as landing and gate steps, not tests). Measured: the 25 pass in 24 s wall, 64 s summed, in a selection run on the same loaded host.
Keep the 25 and also the live-kb checks of test_live_kb.py (17 ids, about 41 s summed): 42 ids in 10 files

notes: Premise, run 2026-10-16 on 168a3a7591: perfcheck.py ids collects 87 ids in 14 files; a profiled whole run (tests.py --durations=0, load 5 to 7 on 14 cores) took 50.3 s wall, 298 s summed per test; the 25 kept ids alone (tests.py -k on their names) passed in 23.9 s wall, 64.5 s summed, on the same host; the last plain whole runs took 29.2 to 31.1 s. The keep list is check 1's set. Fitness (EP-gzr4mmkm) is measured by tool runs, not pytest ids: rag.py eval runs at every landing (land_eval) and check.py and build_index at the sync gate, so test_live_kb.py goes whole. Left as is: _tools/fixtures files, conftest.py's SLOW_FIRST names (conftest.py is a guarded runner file) and the dated run in kb/public/python/pytest.md:73 (a kb fact). Serial: one story, since every deletion writes _tools/test_ids_dropped.txt. Checks 2 (perfcheck.py ids --base 168a3a7591 --allow-removed) and 4 (the nine kept files' selection) pass before the work and are kept as guards: every id lost must be recorded as dropped, and the kept tests must still pass once their files lose the others. Referrers left as they are on purpose (comments, no reader that stops the work): _tools/bench_repro.py:52 (test_bench.py named in a comment), _tools/bl_check.py:1188 (a past sprint's example), _tools/conftest.py:46; kb/_self/backlog.md:220 is ST-jkcn4qs4's to reword. Guards that pass before the work: python3 _tools/perfcheck.py ids --base 168a3a7591ea3145a5f8800e9e052a0368231ea1 --allow-removed _tools/test_ids_dropped.txt passes before the work, and so does check 4, the selection run of the nine kept files.
